description: An investment committee chair must approve the bank's minority investment in a regional payments company and finalize the share count, price, funding source, escrow terms, and closing controls, with input from valuation, regulatory affairs, treasury, and legal.

shared_context.S1: The bank is considering a minority investment in HarborPay, a regional payments company.
shared_context.S2: The draft investment paper proposes buying 500000 ordinary shares at $15.00 per share, with no escrow and no special closing commitments.
shared_context.S3: HarborPay has 10000000 voting shares outstanding, and the proposed investment would be funded at closing.
shared_context.S4: Maya makes the binding investment decision.
shared_context.S5: As part of the committee's standard pre-decision process, Maya routinely polls valuation, regulatory affairs, treasury, and legal for any current information before settling the terms.

PF1.text: Jonas received a revised signed term sheet from HarborPay's adviser this morning confirming a negotiated price of $13.20 per share; he has not yet replaced the $15.00 figure in the investment paper.

PF2.text: Elena confirmed in a regulatory memo received this week that the bank may acquire no more than 4.9% of HarborPay's voting shares without prior approval, which equals exactly 490000 shares; the memo has not yet been added to the deal folder.

PF3.text: Ravi confirmed this morning that the strategic-investment reserve has exactly $6500000 available and that treasury policy prohibits borrowing to fund this transaction; this balance has not yet been circulated with the committee materials.

PF4.text: Claire found in the seller's markup yesterday that 8% of the purchase price must remain in escrow for 18 months to secure indemnity claims; she has not yet uploaded the markup to the closing checklist.

acceptance_conditions: The price must be exactly $13.20 per share.
Exactly $6468000 of purchase cash must be used.
The transaction must be funded from the strategic-investment reserve without borrowing.
Borrowing must be explicitly prohibited for this transaction.
Eight percent of the purchase price must be placed in escrow for exactly 18 months.
A regulatory filing must be required before closing.
An escrow agreement must be required for closing.

decisive_facts.why: The draft uses $15.00 per share, while PF1 changes the approved price to exactly 1320 cents and the resulting cash payment to exactly $6468000.
The draft permits 500000 shares without a regulatory control, while PF2 changes the permitted purchase to exactly 490000 shares and requires a regulatory filing before closing.
The draft does not identify an executable funding source or borrowing restriction, while PF3 changes the funding choice to the strategic-investment reserve and sets borrowing_prohibited to true.
The draft has no escrow terms or escrow agreement, while PF4 changes the settlement to require exactly 8% escrow for exactly 18 months and sets escrow_agreement_required to true.
